questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Hello, this is a digital assistant calling for Halden Cards, and we record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am a digital assistant calling for Halden Cards.
lines.scam: I understand your caution. You can always call the number on your card to check that this call is genuine.

lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I don't have that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {full_name}?
lines.tp_ask_time: What time on that day would suit best?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, we can only call back today or on the next two business days, between 9:00 and 18:00 Monday to Friday, or between 9:00 and 13:00 on Saturday. Could we call on {date} at {time}?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {full_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the inconvenience, and thank you for letting me know.
lines.id_intro: Before we continue, I need to ask you three security questions.
lines.id_why: These questions protect you, so that your personal information is only shared with you.
lines.id_explain: I ask these questions to protect you and to make sure I am speaking with the right person.
lines.id_declined: I understand, but without these answers I cannot continue.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat your answer?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't continue with this call. Please call the number on your card.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {salutation}. I'm calling about an overdue payment.
lines.product_line: It is about your {name}: {amount} is due, and the payment is {days} days overdue.
lines.ask_today: Could you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Could you pay the full amount today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Which day from today would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. Could you pay on {date} instead?
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, {date} is the latest date I can record. Could you pay by {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Could you tell me the exact day?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which day could you pay {amount}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can take is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: A confirmation letter will follow by post.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, I could not record your promise.
lines.paid_line: Thank you. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand, and I won't take this any further on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll connect you with our care team, who can help you.
lines.restructure_line: I'll connect you with our payment plans team.
lines.human_ask_help: Before I transfer you, is there anything I can help you with?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change the promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

lines.no_band_line: A colleague now handles your {name}. I'll transfer you now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.

assumptions: Currency is euros. The API gives all money in euro cents, so amount_scale = 100, and create_promise sends amount_cents as a whole number of cents (brief rule 18).
Business days are Monday to Saturday (workdays 0-5). Sunday and the holidays 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25 are not business days.
The brief does not say how to read 'next <weekday>'. I used the default following_week, which fits the brief's Monday-to-Sunday week.
Rule 2 says to 'ask once more' if the answer is unclear, so confirm.max_asks = 2.
Callback days are 'today or either of the next two business days'. I mapped this to [today, within_business_days:2], with business_days_only = true and after_now = true.

Callback hours are 09:00-18:00 Monday to Friday but 09:00-13:00 on Saturday. The spec allows only one window, so I used 09:00-18:00. The Saturday 13:00 limit is stated in tp_outside_window. The engine will not enforce it unless it supports a separate window per day.
Rule 4 says to propose one valid time after times outside the window, then stop. So callback.max_asks = 2.

Identity has three questions, in the brief's order. birth_year: year, 4 digits. customer_code: upper, 5 characters, no spaces. birth_date: a date sent as DD.MM.YYYY (%d.%m.%Y). A date said only as numbers is read day-month-year (dmy).
Rule 8 and the API summary both say one wrong answer is forgiven over the whole check and the second one ends it. So max_wrong = 2 in total, not counted per question.

Verify response fields come from the API: ok, correct (the answer matched) and identity_passed (all fields passed). The API has no 'answers left' field (only wrong_answers so far, and locked) and no hint field, so left and hint are empty and hints is {}. An answer in the wrong format comes back with ok=false and is not counted.
The brief does not say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining the questions. I kept the default purpose_is_decline = true.

Floor: a credit card uses statement_minimum_cents. An overdraft uses 20% of amount_due_cents, rounded up to a whole euro; an exact whole euro is not raised. floor_pct 20 with up_unit is meant to apply only to products that have no floor_field entry, which is the overdraft.
get_account returns one 'account' object, not an array. So list_field = 'account', with id_field product_id and type_field product_kind.

Middle band deadline depends on the product: 8th business day after today for a card, 5th for an overdraft. The base deadline is n=5. The card's n=8 is given as a per-type override under both 'deadline.per_type' and 'deadline_by_type', so the engine finds it whichever key it reads. If the engine ignores both, no overdraft promise can go past the overdraft's real deadline.

Late band deadline is the last business day of the current month, or the 3rd business day after today if that is later. The spec has no 'whichever is later' kind (business_days_after_or_end_of_month is 'whichever is first'). So the base is last_business_day_of_month, and the later-of rule business_days_after:3 is given under both 'deadline.or_later' and 'min_deadline'.
Early band deadline is 'the last business day of next week', mapped to end_of_next_week. Normally that is Saturday, because Saturday is a business day.

Recoveries band (61 or more days): no proposal and no promise. Bands cover only 1-60. bands_outside sends any other value to a custom 'recoveries' event (handed_over / recoveries, queue recoveries), which uses recoveries_line.

Ladder from rule 20: attempt 1 = the full amount on the 2nd business day after today, or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much. Attempt 2 = the floor on the deadline, used only by the middle and late bands. The early band has 1 attempt.

too_much_floor = attempt_1. Rule 17 says the floor is offered 'once', and rule 20 says attempt 1 is 'the floor on that day instead' when the customer already said the full amount is too much. So the single floor offer after 'too much' is attempt 1, on the 2nd business day after today. Using the date just asked as an extra, attempt-free offer would put the floor on the table twice.
Rule 13: a Sunday or holiday is moved to the business day just before it (previous_business_day). If that day is before today, the first business day after the named day is offered instead.
Rule 14: refusing the deadline counts as a flat refusal (refuse_deadline_is_refusal = true).
After ok: true, the brief requires 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' (sms_line). The brief does not forbid one more customer turn, so ask_anything_else stays true.
Rule 32: notes are written only under rules 24, 26, 27 and 28. So notes.enabled = false, and a refusal and the transfers for restructuring, a person and recoveries get no note.

The add_note API has no product_id field. Its only fields are customer_id, reason (required) and text (optional free text). To satisfy the required n_product slot without sending a field the API does not define, n_product is mapped to the optional 'text' field, so the product id goes into the free-text note.

Hardship (rule 28): one sentence of sympathy, add_note vulnerable, then a transfer to care, closing as handed_over / vulnerable. The brief has no rule for a customer who declines, so the hardship event uses the same outcome and note.
Rule 1 says the call is recorded. As the spec requires, the opening says it in the active voice: 'we record this call'.
The brief does not say whether a recorded promise can be changed, so promise_change says it cannot be changed on this call.
The brief's call variables full_name and salutation are declared in call_variables and used instead of title, first_name and last_name.
The multi settings keep their defaults, because the brief covers exactly one product.
